text: At a turn of the road. <break time="0.8s" /> He saw the figure of a man. <break time="0.8s" /> In grave and decent clothes. <break time="0.8s" /> Seated at the foot of an old tree. <break time="0.8s" /> Who rose and walked beside him. <break time="0.8s" /> You are late, Goodman Brown. <break time="0.8s" /> Said the stranger. <break time="0.8s" /> For the clock of the Old South. <break time="0.8s" /> Was striking as I came through Boston. <break time="0.8s" /> And that is full fifteen minutes ago. <break time="0.8s" /> The traveler was about fifty years old. <break time="0.8s" /> And looked so much like Goodman Brown. <break time="0.8s" /> That they might have been taken. <break time="0.8s" /> For father and son. <break time="0.8s" /> The only thing about him. <break time="0.8s" /> That could be fixed upon as remarkable. <break time="0.8s" /> Was his staff. <break time="0.8s" /> Which bore the likeness. <break time="0.8s" /> Of a great black snake. <break time="0.8s" /> And seemed to wriggle. <break time="0.8s" /> Like a living serpent. <break time="0.8s" /> Come, Goodman Brown. <break time="0.8s" /> Said the traveler. <break time="0.8s" /> This is a dull pace. <break time="0.8s" /> For the beginning of a journey. <break time="0.8s" /> So take my staff. <break time="0.8s" /> If you are so soon weary. <break time="0.8s" /> Friend, said the young man. <break time="0.8s" /> Stopping short. <break time="0.8s" /> Having kept my promise. <break time="0.8s" /> By meeting thee here. <break time="0.8s" /> I now intend to return. <break time="0.8s" /> Whence I came. <break time="0.8s" /> For I have scruples. <break time="0.8s" /> About this business. <break time="0.8s" /> My father never went into the woods. <break time="0.8s" /> On such an errand. <break time="0.8s" /> Nor his father before him. <break time="0.8s" /> Said Brown. <break time="0.8s" /> For we have been a race. <break time="0.8s" /> Of honest men and good Christians. <break time="0.8s" /> The traveler replied that he had helped Browns grandfather. <break time="0.8s" /> Whip a Quaker woman. <break time="0.8s" /> Through the streets of Salem. <break time="0.8s" /> And had helped his father. <break time="0.8s" /> Burn an Indian village. <break time="0.8s" /> In King Philips War. <break time="0.8s" /> I have a general acquaintance. <break time="0.8s" /> In New England, he added. <break time="0.8s" /> And the deacons of many a church. <break time="0.8s" /> The selectmen of many a town. <break time="0.8s" /> And even the governor. <break time="0.8s" /> Are firm friends of mine.
